item.title: MacroMicro Even with Jensen Huang back, AI financing issues haven't gone away. T
item.description:
MacroMicro
Even with Jensen Huang back, AI financing issues haven't gone away. The stress has just moved from CoreWeave to Oracle.

Back in late September, Oracle hit developers with a force majeure notice on its New Mexico Jupiter site over gas pipeline and grid permit delays. If the campus isn't online by 2028, Oracle can push back rent payments. The project carries around $18B in debt through a third-party SPV backed by Oracle's long-term lease, which is part of a global bank syndicate construction loan package across three Oracle and OpenAI compute sites: $38B total for Wisconsin (Lighthouse) and Texas (Frontier), plus $18B for Jupiter.

Reports out in November show banks are already offloading this paper. HSBC dumped $300M of Jupiter senior loans at 85 cents on the dollar, ING auctioned a $500M package with Jupiter debt in it, and SocGen is trying to move $300M in Wisconsin and Texas project bonds. Jupiter is really just the trigger here. What the market is actually worried about is Oracle's long-term cash flow and how reliant they are on OpenAI.

After the close last Friday (Nov 20), Oracle put out a rare statement saying they wrapped up their final funding round earlier this month, making them the first hyperscaler "fully funded" for this investment cycle. They claimed everything, vendor financing included, is locked in and delivering on OpenAI contracts won't depend on extra side deals. On the buildout front, they said Abilene (Astra-6) is almost finished, the Shackelford GW-scale site has all its permits, and NVIDIA Vera Rubin racks are arriving in the coming weeks. They also stuck with their target of turning FCF positive in 2H FY28 and hitting over $30B in FCF by FY29. One catch is Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa's earlier call for a data center moratorium, which adds another variable to their expansion plans past 2027-28.

None of it has reassured bondholders, however. Yesterday, Oracle's 6.7% unsecured 2056 bonds slid to 76.295, putting the yield close to 9% and the G-spread (over the 30Y Treasury) at 372.8 bps. 5Y CDS widened past 360 bps, way above the other four hyperscalers: MSFT at 50 bps, GOOGL at 87 bps, AMZN at 98 bps, and META at 119 bps. Credit is clearly repricing Oracle's default risk.

It fits the broader split we're seeing in the bond market, where stress is piling into weaker high yield. CCC to BB spreads are sitting near 1,000 bps, levels we've only seen during the 2020 pandemic, the 2015-16 shale bust, and 2008. Meanwhile, BBB to AA spreads are holding near 50 bps, so IG still looks relatively stable. Part of that comes down to index mix: $AMZN, GOOGL , $META, and $NVDA now make up an estimated 35% of the US AA bond pool, stretching modified duration out to 7.6 years. All that supply is pushing AA spreads wider and squeezing the relative gap against BBBs.
tweet

item.description:
江卓尔_莱比特矿池
刚才破了一下58.8k，
但针不够深，所以不交易，
这种摸针单，要越深的针，
盈利概率越大 ： ）

最近中线很难预测，
我准备主要做一些短线的摸针单。

摸针单：在上下插大针时立即买进去，
（要有大交易量+关键点位），
然后止损设小，总体胜率小于50%，
但胜时盈利>>负时小亏。

大概就如下图，
左边两个箭头的大针都是成功案例，
当然不是插针都摸，
大部分插针完都会继续往前走，
要选择可能反转的关键点位。

例如现在58.8k是61.8%和前低的关键点，
一般认为跌不破会继续反弹，
跌破会去55k找支撑。

摸针单不预测会不会跌破，
只是在这位置插大针时抄进去，
直接洞穿，不V反插针，
或者跌不到，就不交易。

抄进去后，止损设针底等很近的位置，
期望值是小亏大赚。

刚才写了一长段原理介绍、技巧和历史战绩统计，
但考虑到这个策略容量很有限，
100~200BTC就很难开单了，
所以就不详细说了 ： ） - 江卓尔_莱比特矿池
tweet
